jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Industrial Compute organization is building and operating the infrastructure required to support frontier AI at unprecedented scale. The organization works across data center development, power, design and construction, hardware, supply chain, deployment, facilities operations, and external partnerships. As this infrastructure footprint grows, OpenAI must ensure that sustainability, operational reliability, and responsible development are incorporated into infrastructure decisions from the beginning rather than addressed as separate downstream initiatives. About the Role We are seeking an Infrastructure Operations & Sustainability Lead to develop and execute the sustainability strategy for OpenAI’s global infrastructure portfolio. This role will translate environmental priorities and external commitments into practical operating requirements across site selection, data center design, construction, equipment procurement, deployment, and ongoing operations. You will build the frameworks, metrics, governance, and cross-functional programs required to improve environmental performance while preserving the speed, reliability, and scalability demanded by OpenAI’s infrastructure roadmap. The role will partner closely with infrastructure operations, site development, engineering, construction, power, hardware, supply chain, finance, legal, public policy, government affairs, communications, and external infrastructure partners. This is a senior leadership role requiring infrastructure fluency, sustainability expertise, executive judgment, and the ability to drive complex initiatives across organizational boundaries. Key Responsibilities - Develop and maintain a comprehensive sustainability strategy for OpenAI’s global compute infrastructure. - Translate sustainability objectives into actionable requirements for site selection, design, construction, procurement, commissioning, and operations. - Establish decision frameworks that balance environmental impact with infrastructure reliability, deployment speed, cost, and scalability. - Develop strategies addressing operational and embodied carbon, water stewardship, materials, construction impacts, waste, circularity, and equipment lifecycle management. - Partner with data center engineering and operations teams to identify practical improvements in infrastructure efficiency, resource use, resilience, and operational performance. - Incorporate sustainability considerations into self-build, colocation, cloud, and strategic infrastructure-partner decisions. - Establish measurable goals, operating metrics, dashboards, and governance mechanisms for infrastructure sustainability programs. - Improve the quality, consistency, and auditability of environmental and operational data across internal teams and external partners. - Work with hardware, manufacturing, and supply chain teams to develop supplier requirements and lifecycle strategies for infrastructure equipment. - Evaluate emerging technologies, design approaches, and operating practices and determine which should move from pilot programs into scaled deployment. - Develop business cases that clearly communicate environmental impact, implementation requirements, cost, schedule, and operational tradeoffs. - Partner with Public Policy and Government Affairs on infrastructure-related sustainability positions, regulatory developments, and external engagement. - Represent OpenAI in conversations with infrastructure partners, industry organizations, policymakers, community stakeholders, and other external parties. - Provide executive leadership with clear assessments of progress, material risks, strategic choices, and recommended actions. - Build repeatable playbooks that allow sustainability practices to scale across sites, geographies, infrastructure partners, and technology generations. Qualifications - 12+ years of experience in sustainability, infrastructure operations, environmental strategy, data center infrastructure, the built environment, or a related field. - Experience leading sustainability or operational-improvement programs across a large, complex, and geographically distributed organization. - Demonstrated ability to translate high-level environmental objectives into practical engineering, procurement, construction, and operational requirements. - Strong understanding of carbon, water, materials, waste, circularity, and lifecycle considerations within physical infrastructure. - Experience building metrics, governance systems, and executive reporting for complex operational programs. - Ability to evaluate technical, financial, environmental, regulatory, and reputational tradeoffs together. - Strong cross-functional leadership and the ability to influence senior stakeholders without relying on direct authority. - Experience working with external partners, suppliers, regulators, policymakers, or industry organizations. - Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to make complex subjects clear and decision-ready for executives. - Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment with incomplete information, changing priorities, and significant external scrutiny. Preferred Skills - Experience with hyperscale data centers, cloud infrastructure, industrial facilities, or another power- and resource-intensive operating environment. - Familiarity with data center design, construction, facilities operations, hardware supply chains, and infrastructure-development lifecycles. - Experience with embodied-carbon reduction, sustainable construction materials, water-positive programs, equipment circularity, or infrastructure-efficiency initiatives. - Knowledge of greenhouse-gas accounting, environmental disclosure frameworks, lifecycle assessment, and sustainability-related data systems. - Experience developing external partnerships or industry initiatives that produced measurable operational outcomes. - Familiarity with energy procurement and utility policy sufficient to partner effectively with dedicated power and energy teams. - Experience building or leading multidisciplinary sustainability and infrastructure programs through periods of rapid organizational growth. ABOUT THE ROLE The Lead Corporate Security Engineer will be our domain expert for securing our Corporate IT environment. You’ll work closely with colleagues in IT, Business Systems, Security, and Engineering to ensure that our corporate systems are implemented and maintained securely. As a senior member of the team, your impact will be split between building your team, enabling others, and doing hands-on work to mature our systems, processes, and behaviors. You'll lead the corporate security domain end to end: identity and access governance, endpoint and vulnerability management, detection and response, third-party integration risk, vendor assessment, and SaaS posture. You'll set the standard, own the roadmap, and be accountable for the outcome. IT Engineering runs the platforms day to day and are your closest partners. HOW THIS ROLE WORKS WITH IT Ownership splits by layer, not by system. IT Engineering owns the run; you own the standard and the direction. - You set the corporate security roadmap. What we secure, in what order, to what bar with buy-in from leadership and XFN stakeholders - IT engineering owns platform operations. Our SaaS portfolio is administered and integrated by them. You define what those platforms must enforce - You raise the bar around you. You make your reasoning explicit so that partners make good security calls without you in the room, and you build the tooling and defaults that make the secure path the default path WHAT YOU'LL OWN Identity and access governance - Own the access model at Suno: the RBAC and entitlement design, least-privilege defaults, and the governance layer in Lumos that enforces them - Set the standard for what access review, certification, and approval should look like here — then build toward it rather than importing someone else's framework - Drive access lifecycle automation so joiner/mover/leaver is correct by default and exceptions are visible - Get ahead of non-human identity: service accounts, agents, and automations are a growing share of what holds access at Suno, and we need a model for them before it's urgent Endpoint security and vulnerability management - Own the security standard for our fleet: hardening baseline, compliance signals, device trust, and how endpoint posture feeds access decisions - Own third-party vulnerability management as a program — coverage, risk-based remediation SLAs, reporting, and the negotiation with teams whose tools are the problem - Partner with the IT engineer who owns Kandji so the standard becomes deployed policy without degrading how people work Detection and response - Own our EDR deployment and maintenance - Collaborate with Detection and Response on corporate security incidents to closure Third-party and integration risk - Own how Suno evaluates third-party access: integration and OAuth review for Slack, Google Workspace and the rest of the portfolio, plus vendor security assessment at purchase and renewal - Define our risk appetite in practice and make it legible enough that others apply it without you - Turn recurring decisions into policy, scope guidance, and tooling so the review queue shrinks as the company grows SaaS security posture - Build and own the program: the bar for our SaaS applications, the assessment cadence, and the remediation that follows - Improve tenant-level configuration across the portfolio — SSO and SCIM coverage, MFA and session policy, admin role hygiene, OAuth grant and token management, data sharing defaults Cross-functional leadership - Work with IT, Security, Engineering, AI Enablement, and Legal to shape how Suno builds and buys - Influence the scope of what comes next: how our GRC function plugs in, what we automate versus staff, where the next investment goes - Mentor and raise the technical bar for people around you, including partners who aren't security specialists WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE - First 90 days: you've formed your own view of our security posture, built working relationships with the IT engineers the broader Security team, and told us the three things we're wrong about - First 6 months: a corporate security roadmap exists that IT and the CISO are aligned behind, with the sequencing and the tradeoffs made explicit; the highest-risk items are already moving - First year: entitlement sprawl and vulnerability backlog are measurably down, detection reflects our real risks, third-party review is fast enough that nobody routes around it, and the standard holds because it's built into tooling and shared judgment rather than into you WHAT YOU'LL BRING - ~8+ years in corporate/enterprise security or security engineering, including having owned identity, endpoint, or SaaS security as a domain rather than as a set of tickets - Deep hands-on expertise with a modern IdP and with IGA or access-governance tooling (Lumos, Veza, ConductorOne, Opal, or similar) - You've designed an entitlement or RBAC model across a large SaaS portfolio and lived with the consequences long enough to know what breaks - Endpoint security depth in a macOS-primary fleet: MDM-delivered hardening, compliance and device trust, third-party patch and vulnerability management at scale - Strong command of OAuth, SAML, OIDC, and SCIM, and of the risk model behind third-party integrations - A track record of setting a security standard that other people applied without you enforcing it — written policy, tooling, defaults, or all three - Experience influencing engineering and business teams who don't report to you, early enough in their process to change the outcome - Automation fluency: Python or TypeScript, REST APIs, and a habit of building integrations and internal tooling as a normal part of the job - Excellent writing and judgment under ambiguity. You can hold a position with an executive and change it when the evidence says to - A calibrated sense of risk and how to communicate likelihood, impact, and tradeoffs Helpful, not required: insider risk or DLP programs, zero-trust network access, SOC 2 or ISO program ownership, just-in-time access patterns or identity-as-code, securing AI agent and non-human identity access, prior experience as the first or second security hire at a fast-growing company. HOW WE LEVEL THIS ROLE This is an L6 individual contributor role. At Suno, L6 means you shape how a domain operates cross-functionally and set the standard of excellence within it. You identify problems before they become systemic or are named by others. jobs.description: We're hiring a Sr. Technical Infrastructure Program Manager to build the physical hardware designs that harden IT workstations across Amazon's fulfillment network - 30,000+ stations per year across hundreds of buildings globally. The work is mechanical design at scale: you pull a building's layout, assess whether our standardized station components fit, engineer modifications where they don't, and deliver a documented design package that vendors can build and field teams can install - right the first time. The challenge is precision and consistency across hundreds of building variations, tight cyclical deployment windows, and near-zero tolerance for rework - because an error at design cascades to thousands of stations. You'll join a new team that's building its engineering processes from scratch. We need someone who brings best practices from industry - documentation standards, design validation rigor, cross-functional communication habits - and helps us build the playbook as we scale. Key job responsibilities - Pull building CAD/layout files for upcoming and previous deployments and assess whether existing standardized station components fit the space. Engineer modifications (SolidWorks step files, drawings) where they don't. - Deliver documented, locked design packages to deployment teams - specs, BOM, install guides, and constraints clear enough that a 3PL crew can install without calling you. - Write component specifications to a standard that multiple vendors can compete on - enabling supply chain to run RFPs rather than sole-sourcing custom parts. - Conduct field fit assessments at fulfillment sites (~35% travel) - validate designs against real building conditions, identify issues before they become deployment blockers. - Track design milestones against cyclical funding and installation windows - the deployment calendar is fixed, and designs must be ready before the window opens or we miss the opportunity. - Build and maintain design documentation, validation records, and fit assessment results - contribute to the team's standards and engineering process as we build it from scratch. - Collaborate cross-functionally with launch teams (understanding what's been deployed historically and what variation exists), supply chain (pricing and sourcing), and deployment engineers (install execution and feedback). - Identify potential design issues early - an error not caught at the design stage delays a multi-year program. A day in the life Your morning might start with a batch of building layouts for 5 sites scheduled to deploy next quarter. You open SolidWorks, pull in the station CAD, and overlay it against each building's floor plan - 3 fit perfectly with our standard components, 1 needs a bracket modification for a column obstruction, and 1 has a cable routing conflict you need to solve. You document the 3 clean fits, design the bracket mod, and flag the cable routing issue for a field assessment next week. After lunch you're on a call with a vendor reviewing first samples against your spec - checking dimensions and material before approving a production run. Later you're updating your milestone tracker because a funding window shifted and two designs need to accelerate. You Slack the deployment engineer to confirm the updated timeline works for their site schedule. Before you leave, you check in with your peer engineer on a shared component that both of your designs use - confirming you're both specifying the same version. About the team OTS ACES Solution Design owns the physical workstation infrastructure across Amazon's fulfillment network - we design it, deploy it, and prove it works. We're a new team building our engineering processes as we scale from thousands to tens of thousands of stations per year. We value people who bring industry best practices, document their work so others can build on it, and communicate early when something isn't right. Our culture is direct, ownership-driven, and biased toward building systems rather than heroic individual effort.
